summary: Private install lacks clear latency dashboards; customer requests baseline panels + recommended thresholds
description:
Customer (HelioBank) is running Redwood Private in their VPC and reports that they do not have a clear way to (a) see end-to-end request latency and (b) determine whether high latency is coming from gateway vs runtime prefill vs decode vs queueing.

They are asking Redwood Support for:
1) Recommended baseline latency dashboards/panels (Grafana) that Redwood considers “day-1 usable” for Private.
2) Recommended default thresholds (at least starter values) for p95/p99 latency and error rate to use in alerts.
3) Guidance on which dimensions to break down by (route/model/tenant) without causing Prometheus cardinality issues.

---
Issue summary
- No single dashboard in their current setup answers: “Is latency regression due to queueing, GPU saturation, or upstream gateway timeouts?”
- Existing dashboards are generic Kubernetes/node exporter views; Redwood service metrics are present but not organized.

Impact
- Operators cannot quickly triage customer-facing latency complaints.
- Support escalation risk: “we can’t tell if it’s Redwood or our network.”

Environment details (per customer / TAM notes)
- Deployment mode: Private (customer-managed VPC)
- Kubernetes: EKS 1.29
- Prometheus: kube-prometheus-stack (customer managed)
- Grafana: customer managed (OAuth via Okta)
- Redwood components: gateway + runtime + control plane installed via Redwood Private installer
- Observed workload: ~35–60 RPS peak, mix of streaming + non-streaming chat completions

What they have tried
- Built an ad-hoc Grafana panel using histogram_quantile() over gateway request latency, but don’t know which labels/dimensions are safe to use.
- Tried alerting on p95 latency > 2s for 5m; too noisy during batch jobs and rollouts.

Request from customer
- A concrete list of recommended panels and “starter thresholds” to align their go-live checklist with Redwood’s support expectations.

Support triage notes
- This is not an outage (no active Sev1). Request is for baseline guidance and standardization.
- Likely resolved by providing the Private Observability Minimum Pack dashboard catalog + alert philosophy and confirming required metric names/labels.
- If customer is missing metrics/labels, follow-up may be needed with telemetry instrumentation owners.

Next actions
- Provide panel inventory + example PromQL queries.
- Provide initial threshold guidance: availability/error SLOs, latency SLI selection, and burn-rate alerting recommendations.
- Confirm safe dimensions: route/model/tenant guidance aligned with cardinality constraints.
comments: 2025-01-29 (Owen Phillips - Support): Acknowledged request. Looping in Dev Patel (Support readiness) + Allison Grant (observability standards) for recommended baseline panels + starter thresholds. Can you confirm whether you’re using Redwood’s observability pack assets or purely customer-managed dashboards today?

2025-01-30 (Customer - HelioBank SRE): We are not using Redwood-provided dashboards. We scrape metrics from the gateway and runtime via ServiceMonitors, but our Grafana is mostly generic. Main need is latency breakdown (queue vs inference) and threshold guidance we can defend to internal stakeholders.

2025-01-30 (Dev Patel - Support): Thanks. For Private, Redwood’s current recommendation is to provision the “Private observability minimum pack” dashboards (Grafana JSON + standard templates). Even if you keep customer-managed Grafana, you can import the dashboards into a folder and point them at your Prometheus data source.

Baseline dashboards we recommend (day-1):
1) Gateway / Service Overview: RPS, p50/p95/p99, 4xx/5xx, upstream timeouts, streaming disconnect rate.
2) Runtime Performance: prefill vs decode latency, tokens/sec, batch size distribution, queue depth, KV cache hit rate.
3) GPU Saturation: GPU util %, GPU mem %, throttling (if exported), correlate with p99 latency.
4) Control plane health (if you run control plane services in-cluster): config/policy store health, routing/fallback counters.

I’ll follow up with PromQL examples and initial thresholds; we generally recommend burn-rate alerting over static p99 thresholds to reduce noise.

2025-01-31 (Allison Grant - SRE/Observability): Adding notes on dimensions/cardinality. For Private supportability, the “safe by default” breakdown is:
- route (small bounded set; OK)
- model (bounded set, but beware frequent canary variants; OK if limited)
- tenant: only if you have a small, bounded tenant set; avoid high cardinality tenant_id if it can explode (recommend grouping to “tenant_tier” or “workspace” if stable/bounded).

If you want per-tenant views, prefer logs/tracing sampling rather than Prometheus label explosion. Also avoid labeling raw request_id in metrics.

For latency, choose a consistent SLI:
- End-to-end request latency (gateway) for user experience
- Runtime inference latency (prefill/decode) for capacity/perf triage
- Queue time (scheduler/runtime) for saturation diagnosis

2025-02-03 (Dev Patel - Support): Providing starter thresholds (to be tuned to your workload):

A) Availability / errors (recommended to alert first)
- 5xx rate: page if error ratio > 1% for 10m OR burn-rate multi-window (e.g., 2% for 5m AND 0.5% for 1h depending on your SLO).
- Request failures (non-2xx excluding expected 4xx): warn at 0.5% for 15m; page at 1% for 10m.

B) Latency (warn + investigate; page only when paired with error or SLO burn)
- Gateway p95 latency: warn if > 2.5s for 15m (streaming endpoints should be tracked separately; consider time-to-first-token if available).
- Gateway p99 latency: investigate if > 5s for 10m (treat as symptom; page if also correlated with error ratio or saturation).

C) Saturation / queueing (early indicators)
- Runtime queue depth: investigate if sustained > N (N depends on replica count; start with > 2x replicas for 10m).
- GPU util: if > 90% for 15m AND p99 latency rising, treat as capacity issue.

If you want, we can review a 24h snapshot of your current p95/p99 to tune these to your baseline. The minimum pack alerting philosophy is to avoid paging on raw p99 unless it correlates with SLO burn or customer-visible failures.

2025-02-03 (Customer - HelioBank SRE): This is helpful. We need example queries for the latency panels (gateway histogram_quantile, runtime prefill/decode). Also: do you have a recommended split for streaming vs non-streaming?

2025-02-04 (Dev Patel - Support): Example PromQL patterns (adjust metric names to match your current exporter; if you share your exact metric names we’ll tailor):

1) Gateway request p95 (end-to-end)
- histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, route) (rate(redwood_gateway_request_duration_seconds_bucket{status=~"2.."}[5m])))

2) Gateway error ratio
- sum(rate(redwood_gateway_requests_total{status=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(redwood_gateway_requests_total[5m]))

3) Runtime prefill vs decode latency (if exported as separate histograms)
- histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, model) (rate(redwood_runtime_prefill_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])))
- histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, model) (rate(redwood_runtime_decode_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])))

4) Queue time / queue depth (depending on what you scrape)
- avg_over_time(redwood_runtime_queue_depth[5m]) by (model)

Streaming vs non-streaming: we recommend separate dashboards/panels because “end-to-end” latency is not comparable. Track:
- Streaming: time-to-first-token + stream disconnect rate
- Non-streaming: full response latency (p95/p99)

If you don’t currently have time-to-first-token, we can confirm whether your installed version exports it; otherwise, you can approximate with gateway first-byte metrics if present.

Also sharing links to Redwood’s dashboard catalog + alerting thresholds doc (internal names):
- private-min-pack-dashboard-catalog
- private-min-pack-alerting-philosophy-and-thresholds

2025-02-05 (Owen Phillips - Support): Checking in: do you want us to schedule a 30-min working session to map your current metric names to the minimum pack dashboards and ensure the panels load cleanly in your Grafana/OAuth setup? We’ve seen Grafana folder permissions cause import failures in some private environments.

2025-02-06 (Customer - HelioBank SRE): We imported the suggested dashboards into a new folder and updated the Prometheus data source. The gateway overview and runtime breakdown are now giving us what we needed. We’ll start with the recommended thresholds and tune after a week of baseline collection. You can close this ticket.
resolution: Provided customer with recommended baseline latency dashboards/panels (gateway overview + runtime prefill/decode + GPU saturation) and starter threshold guidance aligned with Redwood’s Private observability minimum pack philosophy. Shared PromQL examples and guidance on safe label dimensions to avoid cardinality blowups. Customer successfully imported dashboards into their customer-managed Grafana and confirmed visibility is sufficient for go-live.
next_steps: If HelioBank requests deeper per-tenant breakdowns, recommend log-based or trace-based sampling rather than adding high-cardinality metric labels. Offer follow-up to tune burn-rate alerts after 7 days of baseline data collection.
